paragraphs: To test their new labels, two members searched for leaves from one tree after a storm. Some photographs had no date, so they could not safely use them to describe a change over time. Instead of guessing, the students marked the missing information and kept those images available for other questions. They also wrote down how each label had been chosen. A later member could then understand the grouping and challenge a decision without losing the original evidence. A useful system needed both flexible categories and records of their limits.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・不定詞・動名詞と分類の限界を読み、比較の条件を理解する。

paragraphs: At the next workshop, Bea asked her partner to summarize the main claim before discussing individual sentences. The summary differed from what Bea had intended, even though the reading had sounded smooth. She realized that a text could be easy to say but still lead a reader toward the wrong conclusion.

She revised the opening and tried the summary task again. This time, her partner identified the intended claim. Bea kept both checks in her routine: listening for difficult sentences and asking what message another person actually received. Each check answered a different question about the draft.
rationale: 間接疑問・比較・譲歩と動名詞を読み、音の滑らかさと意味の伝達を区別する。

paragraphs: After a month, the organizer asked members whether the reflection board was useful. One student said that writing a thoughtful comment every week had begun to feel like another competition. The club made sharing optional and allowed members to keep a reflection private. It also stopped counting how many comments each person posted. A change intended to reduce pressure could create a new kind of pressure if its effects were not checked. The purpose of the record remained helping members choose their next step, rather than collecting impressive reports for everyone else.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・条件節を読み、数値から振り返りに変えても目的の確認が必要だと理解する。

paragraphs: When planning the display, the guide asked workers which examples would be clear to visitors without revealing private production details. They chose a general explanation of a routine safety check and showed where it fitted into the day. The aim was not to suggest that people were constantly rescuing failing machines.

Visitors were asked afterward what had changed in their account of the process. Some now mentioned preparation and monitoring alongside the machines. The guide used these responses to check whether the new display had corrected the earlier impression. Making work visible also required checking what story the audience took away.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・分詞・不定詞を読み、労働の可視化と説明が伝わったかの評価を理解する。

paragraphs: For their next topic, the two friends tried explaining a process before opening their notes. Whenever they could name a stage but not explain the next arrow, they wrote down a question. They then checked the lesson material together instead of filling the gap with a confident guess. After revising the diagram, each friend explained it without the other's help. A shared explanation could sound convincing while one person was doing most of the thinking. Taking separate turns helped them see whether both had understood the links they had drawn.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・条件を含む副詞節を読み、説明の共同修正と個人の理解確認を区別する。
